cards.text: Song of Solomon is a love song between a bride and the one she loves. Right now, something is coming up out of the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant. And a voice asks: who is this?

cards.question: A column of smoke is coming up out of the wilderness, smelling like the finest spices the merchants sell. Who is it?

cards.text: It's Solomon's carriage. That's Solomon, king of Israel, and friend, this king does NOT travel alone.

cards.question: Solomon's carriage is escorted by twelve of the mightiest men of Israel.
All sixty of the warriors around Solomon's carriage are skilled with the sword. Each one keeps his sword at his side so he can salute the king.

cards.text: King Solomon built that carriage out of the timber of Lebanon, with posts of silver, a base of gold and a seat of purple fabric. Friend, I stand on a gold base too, and NOBODY has ever sent sixty warriors to guard it.

cards.question: Solomon's carriage is just as beautiful on the inside. What is its interior inlaid with?

answers.text: Love from the daughters of Jerusalem
Gold from the land of Ophir
Ivory from the ships of Tarshish

cards.text: Then a call goes out for people to come out and gaze at King Solomon. He's wearing a crown, and his own mother is the one who crowned him.

cards.question: Someone is called to come out and gaze at King Solomon in his crown. Who is it?
Solomon's mother crowned him on the day of his ___.

cards.text: The poem gives his wedding day another name: the day of his heart's rejoicing. Friend, back in the junk drawer, a GREAT day was when somebody dug around for the tape and didn't throw anybody out.

Now the groom turns to his bride: “How beautiful you are, my darling—how very beautiful!” Then he describes her one picture at a time: eyes like doves behind her veil, hair like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.

cards.question: The groom says his bride's teeth are like newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing, and “each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.” What is he praising?

cards.text: If I tried lines like that on anybody, friend, I'd be back in the junk drawer by morning. But he's not done: her lips are like a scarlet ribbon, her mouth is lovely, and her brow behind her veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
Then he gets to her neck, and he goes BIG. He pictures something built with rows of stones, with a thousand warriors' shields hanging on it.

cards.question: The groom says his bride's neck is like the ___ of David, with a thousand shields hanging on it.

cards.text: Her breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies. And he says that before the day breaks and the shadows flee, he'll make his way to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.

cards.question: After describing his bride one picture at a time, the groom says she has just one flaw.

cards.text: Now the groom calls out to his bride: “Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon!” He calls her down from the peak of Amana and the summits of Senir and Hermon.

cards.question: The groom also calls his bride down from the dens of the lions and the mountains of the leopards. What kind of place is he calling her away from?

cards.text: Then he calls her “my sister, my bride” and tells her she has captured his heart.

cards.question: The groom says his bride has stolen his heart. He says it took her a long time to win it.

cards.text: One glance of her eyes, one jewel of her neck, and his heart is GONE. Friend, somebody once picked me out of a closing-sale bin for a quarter, and even she had to look twice.

cards.question: The groom says his bride's love is sweet, but not as good as wine.

cards.text: Her lips drip sweetness like the honeycomb, and the fragrance of her garments is like the aroma of Lebanon. Then the picture changes, and he calls her a garden, a spring and a fountain.

cards.question: The groom calls his bride a garden that is open to anyone who wanders in.

cards.text: Then he fills that garden with an orchard of pomegranates and the finest spices, from henna and nard to cinnamon, myrrh and aloes. Friend, I've got six toppings in my whole bakery, and I thought THAT was a lot.
Now he calls her a garden spring, a well of fresh water that comes flowing down.

cards.question: The groom calls his bride a well of fresh water flowing down from ___.

cards.text: Then a call goes out for something to breathe on the garden and spread the fragrance of its spices.

cards.question: What is called on to breathe on the garden and spread the fragrance of its spices?
The call for the winds to breathe on the garden first calls it “my garden.” By the end of that call, the beloved is invited to come in and taste its choicest fruits. Whose garden is it called now?
When the beloved is invited into the garden, the groom answers that he'll come another day.

cards.text: He's come to his garden. He's gathered his myrrh with his spice, eaten his honeycomb with his honey and drunk his wine with his milk.

cards.question: At the end, a voice calls out to the friends for a celebration. What are the friends told to do?

cards.text: “Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved.” Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer where the big party was the dead batteries arguing over who had the most charge left, so THIS is my kind of ending.

findings.problem: David is named for the first time in “the tower of David,” but he is never briefly identified. Papa Dorin should say who David is, such as David, Israel's king.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
